title: Case Study - Virtual Firewall Service
content:
# Case Study - Virtual Firewall Service

## Scenario
A company needs a firewall service that can be deployed dynamically without installing a dedicated physical firewall.

## Architecture
[[Client]]
→ [[SDN Controller]]
→ [[Virtual Firewall]]
→ [[Virtual Router]]
→ [[Server]]

## Main components
- [[NFVO]]
- [[VNFM]]
- [[VIM]]
- [[VNF]]
- [[NFVI]]
- [[SDN Controller]]

## Objective
Deploy the firewall as a VNF, connect it into the traffic path, monitor it, and scale it when required.

title: Case Study Flow
content:
# Case Study Flow

1. [[Service Request]]
2. [[NFVO]] receives/coordinates the service requirement.
3. [[Resource Allocation]] is performed through [[VIM]].
4. [[VNF]] is instantiated by the lifecycle management system.
5. [[SDN Controller]] establishes connectivity.
6. [[Traffic Steering]] sends traffic through the firewall.
7. [[Monitoring and Scaling]] checks performance.
8. If demand increases, [[VNFM]] scales the VNF.
9. [[SDN Controller]] updates connectivity if necessary.
10. When the service ends, the VNF is terminated and resources are released.

title: Client
content:
# Client
Traffic source in the virtual firewall case study.

Connected to the [[Service Chain]] through programmable networking.

title: Monitoring and Scaling
content:
# Monitoring and Scaling

Monitoring observes VNF/service performance.

## When scaling is required
Examples:
- Traffic increases
- CPU utilization increases
- Service demand changes

## Cooperation
[[VNFM]] handles VNF lifecycle scaling.
[[NFVO]] coordinates the service-level decision.
[[SDN Controller]] can adjust connectivity when the topology changes.

title: NFV MANO
content:
# NFV MANO
NFV MANO provides management and orchestration for virtualized network services.

## Main components
- [[NFVO]]
- [[VNFM]]
- [[VIM]]

## Relationship
MANO coordinates the lifecycle and resources required by network services and VNFs.

title: NFV
content:
# NFV
Network Function Virtualization runs network functions as software on virtualized infrastructure.

## Examples
- [[VNF]]
- Virtual firewall
- Virtual router
- Virtual load balancer

## Management
- [[NFV MANO]]
- [[NFVO]]
- [[VNFM]]
- [[VIM]]
- [[NFVI]]

## Connected
- [[SDN]]
- [[VNF Lifecycle]]
- [[Network Service]]

title: NFVI
content:
# NFVI
NFV Infrastructure.

Provides the physical and virtual resources required to run VNFs.

## Resources
- Compute
- Storage
- Networking
- Virtualization layer

## Managed through
- [[VIM]]

## Used by
- [[VNF]]

title: NFVO
content:
# NFVO
Network Functions Virtualization Orchestrator.

## Main role
Coordinates network-service orchestration and resource decisions.

## Works with
- [[VNFM]] — VNF lifecycle management
- [[VIM]] — infrastructure/resource management
- [[SDN Controller]] — connectivity and forwarding
- [[Network Service]] — service-level orchestration

## Important
NFVO does not replace VNFM or VIM. They cooperate.

title: Network Service
content:
# Network Service
A network service is a composed service made from one or more VNFs connected in a defined service chain.

## Example
Client → [[Virtual Firewall]] → [[Virtual Router]] → Internet

## Orchestration
[[NFVO]] coordinates the overall service.

## Connectivity
[[SDN Controller]] provides programmable connectivity.

title: Resource Allocation
content:
# Resource Allocation

Before a VNF can run, suitable NFVI resources must be available.

## Resources
- CPU
- RAM
- Storage
- Virtual networking

## Management
[[VIM]] manages infrastructure resources.
[[NFVO]] coordinates resource requirements for the network service.

title: SDN Controller
content:
# SDN Controller
The SDN Controller provides programmable control over network connectivity and forwarding.

## Role in SDN–NFV
- Establishes connectivity between VNFs
- Applies forwarding/traffic-steering rules
- Connects the virtual network functions into a service chain

## Connected
- [[SDN]]
- [[Traffic Steering]]
- [[Service Chain]]
- [[NFVO]]

title: SDN-NFV Integration Model
content:
# SDN-NFV Integration Model

## Why integrate?
NFV provides flexible virtual network functions. SDN provides programmable connectivity between them.

## Cooperation
[[NFVO]] coordinates the service and resource orchestration.
[[VNFM]] manages VNF lifecycle.
[[VIM]] manages infrastructure.
[[SDN Controller]] establishes and changes connectivity.

## Result
Dynamic network services that can be instantiated, connected, monitored, and scaled.

title: SDN
content:
# SDN
Software-Defined Networking separates network control from forwarding.

## Key ideas
- Centralized/programmable control
- Network programmability
- Dynamic forwarding rules
- Separation of control plane and data plane

## Connected
- [[SDN Controller]]
- [[Traffic Steering]]
- [[SDN-NFV Integration Model]]
- [[NFV]]

title: Server
content:
# Server
Destination/application endpoint in the case study.

Traffic reaches the server after passing through the required [[Service Chain]].

title: Service Chain
content:
# Service Chain

A service chain defines the ordered path through VNFs.

## Example
Client → [[Virtual Firewall]] → [[Virtual Router]] → [[Virtual Load Balancer]] → Server

## SDN role
[[SDN Controller]] steers traffic through the required VNFs.

## NFV role
[[NFVO]] and [[VNFM]] coordinate deployment and lifecycle.

title: Service Request
content:
# Service Request

The starting point of the case study.

Example requirement:
> Deploy a virtual firewall service for incoming and outgoing traffic.

The request becomes a [[Network Service]] that must be orchestrated and connected.

title: Traffic Steering
content:
# Traffic Steering

Traffic steering directs packets through the required VNFs.

## Controlled by
[[SDN Controller]]

## Used for
- Service chaining
- Firewall insertion
- Load balancing
- Dynamic path changes

## Connected
- [[SDN]]
- [[Service Chain]]
- [[SDN-NFV Integration Model]]

title: VIM
content:
# VIM
Virtualized Infrastructure Manager.

## Role
Manages NFVI resources such as:
- Compute
- Storage
- Virtual networking

## Connected
- [[NFVO]]
- [[NFVI]]
- [[Resource Allocation]]

title: VNF Lifecycle
content:
# VNF Lifecycle

## Flow
[[Service Request]]
→ [[Resource Allocation]]
→ Instantiate
→ Configure
→ Monitor
→ Scale/Update
→ Terminate
→ Release Resources

## Management
[[VNFM]] manages VNF lifecycle operations while [[NFVO]] coordinates the wider network service.

title: VNF
content:
# VNF
Virtual Network Function.

A VNF is a software implementation of a network function running on virtualized infrastructure.

## Examples
- Virtual firewall
- Virtual router
- Virtual load balancer

## Managed by
- [[VNFM]]

## Runs on
- [[NFVI]]

## Connected
- [[VNF Lifecycle]]
- [[Service Chain]]

title: VNFM
content:
# VNFM
VNF Manager.

## Role
Manages the lifecycle of a VNF instance.

## Lifecycle actions
- Instantiate
- Configure
- Monitor
- Scale
- Update
- Terminate

## Connected
- [[NFVO]]
- [[VNF]]
- [[VNF Lifecycle]]

title: Virtual Firewall
content:
# Virtual Firewall

A software-based firewall deployed as a [[VNF]].

## Purpose
- Inspect traffic
- Apply security rules
- Allow or block traffic

## Integration
- Runs on [[NFVI]]
- Lifecycle managed through [[VNFM]]
- Overall service coordinated by [[NFVO]]
- Traffic path controlled by [[SDN Controller]]

title: Virtual Load Balancer
content:
# Virtual Load Balancer

A software load-balancing network function implemented as a [[VNF]].

## Role
Distributes traffic across application servers.

## Connected
- [[Service Chain]]
- [[VNF]]

title: Virtual Router
content:
# Virtual Router

A software router implemented as a [[VNF]].

## Role in case study
Provides routing after traffic passes through the [[Virtual Firewall]].

## Connected
- [[Service Chain]]
- [[VNF]]
- [[SDN Controller]]
